subject: Post-call: LLM infra handshake — SDK auth, routing & telemetry

Subject: Post-call: LLM infra handshake — SDK routing and telemetry next steps

Hi Vivek / team,

Thanks for the call today — useful discussion. Quick recap of what matters most for Pangea Health after our discovery:

- Primary goals: predictable latency for patient-facing flows, deterministic embedding-based retrieval, and reproducible reranker scores for audit.
- Deployment preference: Private (VPC) with optional dedicated pool for peak hours.
- Integration asks: lightweight SDK with managed auth rotation (KMS/HSM), routing rules per region + cost-tier fallback, and stable structured outputs / function/tool calling for our clinical actions.
- Observability: we need propagated trace IDs across services, per-token/compute latency breakdown, and dashboards for request sampling + reranker score distributions.

Concrete asks for next steps:
1) Can you share the SDK auth options and recommended pattern for short-lived credentials (we use KMS/HSM and need to map to our IAM roles)?
2) Example routing policy that handles latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive traffic (we want automated fallback to cheaper model variants during load).
3) Telemetry contract — headers/fields we should include now and an example dashboard.
4) A short sandbox test plan (tenant + sample embedding/rerank workload) we can run in our dev environment.

Please loop in whoever owns telemetry hooks — we want the implementation notes (trace header names, which fields to log, latency breakdown format). Also include any lightweight code snippets for function/tool calling schema if available.

Thanks,
Aditi
Aditi Shah

Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM infra handshake — SDK auth, routing & telemetry

Thanks Aditi — great alignment. Short answers + proposed plan below.

Summary answers:
- SDK auth: we support three modes: long-lived API keys (not recommended for private), short-lived signed tokens (recommended: integration with your KMS to sign short-lived assertions), and mTLS client certs for on-prem. See attached "redwood-sdk-auth-matrix.pdf" for specifics and tradeoffs.
- Routing policy pattern: tenant-level primary route -> region affinity -> model-tier fallback. We can ship a policy that encodes latency SLO and cost budget per tenant; automatic fallback replaces model variant with a compatible quantized/fast variant.
- Structured/tool calling: function-calling style with explicit JSON schema works best. We suggest pinning a schema per action and validating server-side before tool invocation to avoid hallucinated operations.
- Observability: we recommend propagating a single request trace id and a per-call request id; log both and emit a latency-breakdown response header. See Marissa's note below for field names.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners):
1) Telemetry contract draft (Marissa) — deliver sample trace/span schema + dashboard queries by EOD tomorrow.
2) Sandbox test plan (Karthik) — lightweight tenant + 1000 embedding/rerank requests, target P95 latency < 220ms.
3) Auth integration doc (Vivek) — outline of short-lived token flow + example code, pull request to your repo for a quick POC.

I attached the auth matrix and a sample trace-span schema to speed implementation. For the sandbox, we recommend a small dedicated GPU slice for repeatability.

Would you be available for a focused 45-min design workshop next week (we have Tue/Wed windows) — agenda: auth handshake, routing policy example, telemetry contract, and a short demo of reranker scoring reproducibility?

Onward,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sdk-auth-matrix.pdf, sample-trace-span-schema.json

Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM infra handshake — SDK auth, routing & telemetry

Hi Aditi, Vivek — adding the telemetry/observability specifics you can hand to your infra team. Below are the concrete fields / headers we recommend and a short example of the latency-breakdown format.

Recommended headers to propagate (HTTP):
- X-RW-Trace-Id: 64-char hex (single trace id propagated across services)
- X-RW-Request-Id: UUID per API call (useful for logs/drilldown)
- X-RW-Region: region hint (us-west-2 / eu-west-1)

Log fields (structured JSON logs):
- rw.trace_id
- rw.request_id
- client.tenant_id
- client.request_type (embed|generate|rerank|tool-call)
- model.name
- model.variant
- input.seq_len
- output.token_count
- compute.ms
- queue.ms
- network.ms
- reranker.score (if applicable)
- reranker.latency_ms

Latency-breakdown response header (example):
X-RW-Latency-Breakdown: compute=45ms;queue=5ms;network=12ms;postproc=7ms

Dashboard queries (Grafana/Prometheus style):
- P95 request latency by client.tenant_id (filter: client.request_type="embed")
- Reranker score histogram and time-series (labels: model.variant)
- Error rate by step (validation, model, postproc)

Embedding/reranker instrumentation: include embedding vector dim (embed.dim) and a deterministic reranker seed in logs for reproducibility. When you run the sandbox, please include a 1% sample of raw request payloads (PII redacted) so we can correlate scoring anomalies.

Small snippet (example header propagation in Python requests):
```python
headers = {
    "X-RW-Trace-Id": trace_id,
    "X-RW-Request-Id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {short_lived_token}",
}
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
```

I'll attach the trace-span schema we discussed and a proposed MOP agenda. I'll also prepare a short Grafana dashboard template you can import.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
